question: Besides being at least 21 years old, what basic educational credential does RELRA Section 511 require of every broker applicant, apart from the 240-hour real estate instruction requirement?
choice_a: High school graduation, or proof of an education satisfactory to the Commission as equivalent
choice_b: A bachelor's degree in any academic field
choice_c: An associate's degree specifically in real estate or business
choice_d: No separate educational credential is required beyond the 240 hours of instruction
explanation: RELRA Section 511(2) requires a broker applicant to be a 'high school graduate or ... produce proof satisfactory to the commission of an education equivalent thereto,' a separate qualification from the age requirement in 511(1) and the 240-hour instruction requirement in 511(3).
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.511(2) (confirmed via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

question: RELRA Section 511(3) itself -- not just the Commission's implementing regulations -- specifically requires the broker applicant's 240 hours of required real estate instruction to include coursework in which two subject areas?
explanation: RELRA Section 511(3) requires 240 hours of real estate instruction 'in areas of study prescribed by the rules of the commission, which rules shall require instruction in the areas of fair housing and professional ethics' -- a statutory-level mandate distinct from 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(b)(2)'s regulatory breakdown of law/office-management/enumerated-subject credits.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.511(3) (confirmed via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

question: Under RELRA Section 512, besides biographical and character information, what must a broker license application specifically designate?
choice_a: The place of business for which the license is desired
choice_c: The applicant's anticipated commission-split arrangement with future salespersons
choice_d: The specific counties in which the applicant intends to practice
explanation: RELRA Section 512 requires the broker application, submitted in writing on prescribed forms, to designate 'the place of business for which such license is desired,' tying the license itself to a specific office location.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.512 (confirmed via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

question: When a partnership, association, or corporation holds a Pennsylvania broker's license, what does RELRA Section 513 require of the entity's employees who engage in real estate business but are NOT the designated broker of record?
choice_a: They must independently meet the salesperson qualification and application requirements of RELRA Sections 521 and 522
choice_b: Nothing -- only the broker of record needs any license at all
choice_c: They must each independently satisfy the full broker qualifications of Sections 511 and 512
choice_d: They are exempt from licensure as long as they act solely under the broker of record's direct written instructions
explanation: RELRA Section 513 applies Sections 511 and 512's broker qualification and application requirements only to the individual designated as broker of record; other employees of the entity who engage in real estate business must separately meet the salesperson qualifications under Sections 521 and 522.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.513 (confirmed via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

question: For a standard broker's license application, 49 Pa. Code Section 35.222 requires the applicant to submit recommendations from which combination of references?
choice_a: One licensed broker and two property owners in the applicant's county, plus two additional property owners if the applicant moved counties within the past year
choice_b: Three licensed brokers with no minimum years of licensure
choice_c: Five character references of any occupation, none of whom may be real estate licensees
choice_d: A single reference letter from the applicant's employing broker only
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.222 requires a standard broker license applicant to submit recommendations from one licensed broker and two property owners in the applicant's county, with two more property-owner recommendations required if the applicant moved to a different county within the preceding year.

question: Which of the following must an out-of-state broker include with an application for a Pennsylvania RECIPROCAL broker's license under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.222?
choice_a: A verified statement confirming no disciplinary actions and an agreement to be bound by Pennsylvania law, along with certification of active, good-standing status from the home-state licensing authority
choice_b: Proof of Pennsylvania residency established at least 1 year before application
choice_c: A notarized waiver of the right to appeal any future Commission disciplinary action
choice_d: Completion of the full 240-hour Pennsylvania broker education curriculum, with no credit for home-state coursework
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.222 requires a reciprocal broker applicant to hold a current, comparable out-of-state broker's license, provide verified statements confirming no disciplinary actions and agreeing to be bound by Pennsylvania law, and submit certification from the home-state authority confirming the license is active and in good standing.

question: To renew a Pennsylvania reciprocal broker's license, 49 Pa. Code Section 35.255 requires the licensee to submit what, beyond the completed application and renewal fee?
choice_a: A certification that the license is current and in good standing in the state of the licensee's principal place of business
choice_b: Proof of 14 hours of Pennsylvania-specific continuing education, waived for standard licensees
choice_c: A new set of character references identical to those required for an initial standard license
choice_d: Nothing further -- reciprocal renewal has no documentation requirement beyond the fee
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.255 requires a reciprocal licensee renewing a Pennsylvania license to provide the Commission with a certification that the license is current and in good standing in the state of the licensee's principal place of business, in addition to the completed application and fee.

question: May a Pennsylvania reciprocal broker who failed to timely renew the license reactivate it without retaking the examination?
choice_a: Yes, provided the licensee still maintains the equivalent of a current standard license in the state of principal place of business
choice_b: No -- any lapse in a reciprocal license requires retaking both portions of the examination
choice_c: Yes, but only within 10 days of the lapse and regardless of the licensee's out-of-state status
choice_d: No -- a lapsed reciprocal license can never be reactivated under any circumstance
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.255 permits a reciprocal licensee who failed to renew to reactivate without re-examination, so long as the licensee maintains the equivalent of a current standard license in the state where the licensee has a principal place of business.

question: Under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.255, within how many days must a reciprocal licensee notify the Commission after establishing a principal place of business in Pennsylvania, or after failing to maintain the out-of-state license underlying the reciprocal license?
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.255 requires a reciprocal licensee to notify the Commission within 30 days of establishing a principal place of business in Pennsylvania, or of failing to maintain the out-of-state license the reciprocal license depends on, after which the licensee must obtain and comply with the requirements of a standard license (including continuing education) to keep practicing.

question: How many hours of continuing education must a Pennsylvania real estate licensee complete during each two-year license period under RELRA Section 404.1?
explanation: RELRA Section 404.1 requires 'each person licensed pursuant to this act ... to obtain 14 hours of mandatory continuing education during each two-year license period,' applicable to brokers, associate brokers, and salespersons alike.
source_note: RELRA Section 404.1, 'Continuing education' (text confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text); hedge: exact P.S. codification suffix for Section 404.1 not independently re-verified this pass, cited elsewhere in this bank as 63 P.S. Section 455.404a per standard Purdon's '.1'-to-'a' section-suffix convention

question: For how long may a Pennsylvania real estate license be placed on inactive status before the licensee loses the ability to simply reactivate it, and what must the licensee show to reactivate within that window?
choice_a: No more than 5 years, and the licensee must show proof of 14 hours of continuing education to reactivate
choice_b: No more than 2 years, with no continuing education needed to reactivate
choice_c: Indefinitely, with no continuing education required to reactivate at any time
choice_d: No more than 1 year, after which the license is automatically revoked
explanation: RELRA Section 404.1 allows a license to be placed on inactive status for no more than 5 years, and requires the licensee to provide evidence of 14 hours of continuing education to reactivate the license within that period.
source_note: RELRA Section 404.1, 'Continuing education' (text confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text); hedge: exact P.S. codification suffix for Section 404.1 not independently re-verified this pass, cited elsewhere in this bank as 63 P.S. Section 455.404a per standard Purdon's '.1'-to-'a' section-suffix convention

question: What is the application fee for a standard or reciprocal broker's, cemetery broker's, or rental listing referral agent's license under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.203's fee schedule?
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.203's fee schedule lists $75 as the application fee for standard or reciprocal licensure of a broker, cemetery broker, or rental listing referral agent -- separate from the $52/$49 Pearson VUE examination fees and the $65 branch office license fee.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.203 (confirmed via pacodeandbulletin.gov fee schedule)
